title: Tor-independent tensor comparison for a bounded projective complex
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and let A and B be commutative R-algebras. Write Tor_i^R(-,-) for the usual projective-resolution Tor groups [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], and assume Tor_i^R(A,B)=0 for every i>0. Put E=A\otimes_R B. Let Q^\bullet be a bounded cochain complex of A-modules whose terms are finite projective A-modules (each is a direct summand of A^m for some finite m), and let D be a localization of E. Writing Q^\bullet\otimes_R^L B for the left-derived tensor product and Q^\bullet\otimes_A D for the ordinary tensor complex, the canonical map H^i(Q^\bullet\otimes_R^L B)\otimes_E D \longrightarrow H^i(Q^\bullet\otimes_A D) is an isomorphism for every i.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: local affine reduction and Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: For every degree n, Q^n is a finite projective A-module. The Tor-independence hypothesis and [lem-pc-finite-projective-tor-acyclic] therefore give Tor_i^R(Q^n,B)=0 for every i>0.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-termwise-tor-acyclic-derived-tensor] to Q^bullet and B. The canonical derived-to-ordinary tensor map is a quasi-isomorphism, so for every i it identifies H^i(Q^bullet tensor_R^L B) with H^i(Q^bullet tensor_R B).

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: The canonical map E=A\otimes_R B\to D is a localization of E, hence D is a flat E-module [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. The ordinary tensor complex C^\bullet=Q^\bullet\otimes_R B is a bounded complex of E-modules (C^n=Q^n\otimes_A E). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], -\otimes_E D preserves exactness of each sequence C^{i-1}\to C^i\to C^{i+1}, so it carries kernels and images of the differentials to those of C^\bullet\otimes_E D, giving H^i(C^\bullet)\otimes_E D\cong H^i(C^\bullet\otimes_E D) for every i. Degreewise associativity of tensor products gives (Q^n\otimes_R B)\otimes_E D=(Q^n\otimes_A E)\otimes_E D\cong Q^n\otimes_A D, compatibly with differentials. Combined with Step 2, under these identifications the map in the statement is the composite of these isomorphisms, hence an isomorphism for every i.
